UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                    )
    Midcontinent        Independent          System ) Docket No. ER26-3650
    Operator, Inc.                                  )

            MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS OF THE
   NORTH AMERICAN ELECTRIC RELIABILITY CORPORATION, MIDWEST
RELIABILITY ORGANIZATION, RELIABILITY FIRST CORPORATION, AND SERC
                    RELIABILITY CORPORATION

         On August 28, 2026, the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) filed

proposed revisions to MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets

Tariff (“Tariff”) with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (the “Commission” or “FERC”)

to establish certain Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large Loads (the “IRR

Proposal”). 1 The IRR Proposal 2 was MISO’s initial step responding to the Commission’s June

2026 Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act directing MISO

to examine tariff provisions to support the interconnection of large load with the Bulk-Power

System (“BPS”). 3 While acknowledging regional differences and market rules, the Commission

highlighted five categories of focus: (i) efficient transmission service application and study; (ii)

potential cost shifting; (iii) co-location arrangements; (iv) new transmission services for flexible

large loads; and (v) a process to study generating facilities serving electrically proximate large




1
         18 C.F.R. §§ 385.206, 385.212, and 385.214 (2026).
2
         Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large
Loads, Docket No. ER26-3650 (Aug. 28, 2026) [hereinafter IRR Proposal].
3
         See, e.g., Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section
206 of the Federal Power Act, 195 FERC ¶ 61,212 (2026) (“Show Cause Order” or “SCO”). The Commission
issued parallel orders tailored to five other regional transmission organizations/independent system operators
(“RTOs/ISOs”), which are together referred to as the “Show Cause Orders.”

                                                        1
 loads and large co-located load. MISO’s IRR Proposal stated that it intended to promote visibility,

ramp rate, and disturbance ride-through requirements applicable to large loads.

         Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, the North American Electric Reliability

Corporation (“NERC”), Midwest Reliability Organization (“MRO”), ReliabilityFirst Corporation

(“RF”), and SERC Reliability Corporation (“SERC”) (collectively, “NERC and the Regional

Entities”) move to intervene and comment on the IRR Proposal. 4 NERC and all six Regional

Entities (collectively, the “ERO Enterprise”) are dedicated to ensuring effective and efficient

reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid, including supporting entities in

identifying and mitigating potential threats to BPS reliability.

         North America is entering a period of unprecedented load growth, with NERC Long-Term

Reliability Assessments (“LTRAs”) noting that demand is higher than at any point in the last two

decades. 5    This projected increase in North American electricity demand is largely driven by

computational load, such as data centers for artificial intelligence and other uses underpinning the

digital economy, interconnecting with the BPS. 6 MISO’s IRR Proposal states, for example, that,


4
          NERC accomplishes its mission with the support of the six Regional Entities who help NERC support
reliability across various interconnections with differing needs and characteristics. The six Regional Entities are
MRO, Northeast Power Coordinating Council, Inc., RF, SERC, Texas Reliability Entity, Inc., and Western
Electricity Coordinating Council. NERC’s relationship with the Regional Entities is governed by Regional
Delegation Agreements or “RDAs” filed with the Commission every five years. 18 C.F.R. § 39.8.
5
         NERC, 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment (Jan. 2026), https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/our-
work/assessments/nerc_ltra_2025.pdf [hereinafter 2025 LTRA]; NERC, 2024 Long- Term Reliability Assessment at
8 (Dec. 2024, updated July 2025),
https://www.nerc.com/pa/RAPA/ra/Reliability%20Assessments%20DL/NERC_Long%20Term%20Reliability%20
Assessment_2024.pdf. NERC develops the Long-Term Reliability Assessments annually in accordance with the
NERC Rules of Procedure and Title 18, § 39.112 of the Code of Federal Regulations; this is also required by Section
215(g) of the Federal Power Act, which instructs NERC to conduct periodic assessments of the North American
BPS.
6
         Id. Please note, in using the term computational load, NERC references that term as used in its assessments
and draft registry criteria and Reliability Standard work. MISO’s IRR Proposal includes MISO’s definition of
computational load which may have differences.


                                                           2
 “[a]s NERC has observed [in the LTRA], the largest contributor to this accelerated demand growth

is data center additions, with 18 GW of data center loads projected [in MISO] by 2035.” 7

        The ERO Enterprise has been working urgently with stakeholders on clear and consistent

measures to support the reliable interconnection of computational loads. As outlined in NERC’s

large load action plan, these efforts include revisions to NERC registry criteria and Reliability

Standards for submission to the Commission by year-end, and further efforts such as disturbance

ride-through performance requirements are underway with filing(s) to the Commission targeted in

2027. MRO, RF, and SERC are the NERC Regional Entities which support activities in the MISO

area. Therefore, NERC and the Regional Entities move to intervene and comment to provide

information on the record regarding efforts to harmonize these activities with those being led by

stakeholders, such as MISO, under parallel processes. 8




7
         IRR Proposal, at 5 (citing the 2025 LTRA, at 15).
8
         These comments are focused only on matters as related to section 215 of the FPA, the ERO Enterprise
declines to comment on matters outside of its purview.

II.       MOTION TO INTERVENE

          NERC and the Regional Entities have a substantial interest in this proceeding as the IRR

Proposal includes market rules which would complement their activities under section 215 of the

FPA. 10 By enacting the Energy Policy Act of 2005 and section 215 of the FPA, 11 Congress

entrusted the Commission with approving and enforcing rules to ensure the reliability of the BPS,


9
         Persons to be included on the Commission’s service list are identified by an asterisk. NERC respectfully
requests a waiver of the Commission’s rules 18 C.F.R. § 385.203 (2016) to allow the inclusion of more than two
persons on the service list.
10
         See, e.g., IRR Proposal, at 3.
11
         16 U.S.C. § 824o.


                                                       4
 and with certifying an Electric Reliability Organization (“ERO”) charged with developing and

enforcing mandatory Reliability Standards, subject to Commission approval. The Commission

certified NERC as the ERO in 2006. 12 As the ERO, NERC’s mission is to ensure effective and

efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. 13

        NERC is responsible for developing and enforcing mandatory Reliability Standards

applicable to BPS entities on NERC’s compliance registry and conducting assessments of the

reliability and adequacy of the BPS. 14 NERC develops Reliability Standards in accordance with

Section 300 (Reliability Standards Development) of the NERC Rules of Procedure (“ROP”) and

the NERC Standard Processes Manual. 15 NERC’s compliance registry includes those entities

which meet registry criteria under Section 500 and Appendix 5B of the ROP. The ERO Enterprise

is responsible for monitoring, assessing, and enforcing compliance with Reliability Standards in

the United States in accordance with Section 400 (Compliance Enforcement) of the ROP and the

NERC Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program. 16

        Since 2024, the ERO Enterprise has been assessing how to address potential issues

associated with large levels of computational load interconnecting with the BPS. As discussed in

NERC comments, as supplemented, on the Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on reforms

 to ensure timely and orderly interconnection of large loads, 17 NERC has been actively pursuing an

accelerated action plan to develop (i) technical justification; (ii) registry criteria updates to the

ROP; and (iii) Reliability Standards to account for computational load. 18 On July 16, 2026 (the

“July 16th Order”), the Commission directed NERC to file registry criteria and Reliability

Standards to address computational load by December 31, 2026. 19 The Commission also directed

NERC to file a work plan by March 1, 2027, detailing next steps for additional Reliability

Standards pertaining to computational load integration. As a result, no other party can adequately

represent NERC and the Regional Entities’ interests in this proceeding. Therefore, the parties

request that the Commission grant this motion to intervene and comment as within the public

interest.

III.    COMMENTS

        Consistent with the July 16th Order, the ERO Enterprise has prioritized near-term measures,

such as foundational Reliability Standards and registry criteria addressing computational loads,

while preserving flexibility for subsequent refinements, such as plans to develop ride-through

requirements next year, as additional experience is gained with large load interconnections. 20 The

ERO Enterprise is working as quickly as possible with stakeholders to advance integration of

computational load in a manner that sustains continued reliability and resilience. Based on risk


17
         Department of Energy, Secretary of Energy’s Direction that FERC Initiate Rulemaking Procedures and
Proposal Regarding the Interconnection of Larg Loads Pursuant to the Secretary’s Authority Under Section 403 of
the Department of Energy Organization Act (Oct. 23, 2025) (“ANOPR”); Interconnection of Large Loads to the
Interstate Transmission Sys., Notice Inviting Comments, Docket No. RM26-4-000 (Oct. 27, 2025).
18
         Comments of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation in Response to Notice Inviting
Comments, Docket No. RM26-4-000 at 1-2, 5-6 (Nov. 21, 2025) (“NERC ANOPR Comments”); NERC Additional
Comments on Large Loads ANOPR (March 20, 2026) (“Supplemental ANOPR Comments”).
19
         Order Directing the North American Electric Corporation to File Reliability Standard(s) Pertaining to
Computational Load Integration, 196 FERC ¶ 61,031 (2026) [hereinafter July 16th Order]. See also, 16 U.S.C. §
824o(d)(5).
20
         July 16th Order at P 11.


                                                       6
 prioritization, the ERO Enterprise and others are working towards foundational expectations to

mitigate the immediate reliability risks associated with computational load. MISO’s filing is an

example of contributions by those across the electric and computational load industries to advance

reliability in the face of this change. Due to the urgency of these near-term measures, the ERO

Enterprise, MISO, and other stakeholders working to mitigate risk are acting in parallel rather than

sequentially, creating potential for some differences. While all stakeholders collaborate to

minimize these differences, different timelines and internal governance processes may yield

slightly different outcomes.

        Regardless of the parallel development, MISO’s IRR Proposal seems generally consistent

with pending Reliability Standards efforts. The ERO Enterprise and RTO/ISO stakeholders,

including MISO, have forums and groups established to continue ensuring consistency to the

extent possible. For example, NERC’s Reliability and Security Technical Committee (“RSTC”)

subgroups, computational load drafting team Project 2026-02, the short-term advisory group for

foundational standards, and an ERO Enterprise and RTO/ISO computational load advisory group

provide crucial input to help synchronize and harmonize parallel efforts advance. In particular,

the RTO/ISO computational load advisory group was developed and designed to foster

coordination on these issues, with a specific focus on the potential performance requirements for

computational loads across interconnections. 21

         Through parallel processing, extensive and extraordinary stakeholder outreach, and

carefully organized comment periods, NERC is striving to rapidly advance reliability and

consistency as knowledge grows. Despite the urgent and parallel actions, the ERO Enterprise has



21
         NERC’s large loads action plan webpage provides further examples of outreach and coordination,
https://www.nerc.com/initiatives/large-loads-action-plan.

                                                       7
 retained a transparent     stakeholder process with robust industry involvement, including

computational load entities, that facilitates further harmonization across actions. At each step of

the pending project for foundational Reliability Standards, the ERO Enterprise expedited processes

where feasible, while maintaining transparency and effective consensus-building through a

concerted effort to involve computational load entities in the standards development process. At

the inception of the Reliability Standards development project, for example, NERC’s Standards

Committee appointed a drafting team based on diverse industry experts that included

computational load entities, RTOs/ISOs, and members of NERC Standing Committees. In light

of the July 16th Order, the Standards Committee also granted waivers to permit shorter balloting

and comment periods in the standards development process. Recently, the RSTC applied expedited

processing for a computational load disturbance ride-through performance Standard Authorization

Request in anticipation of presenting the request to the Standards Committee in the fall of 2026.

The RSTC meetings in September included multiple presentations on the work being done to study

and respond to the needs associated with computational load.

       The ERO Enterprise anticipates that industry will continue to rapidly refine its

understanding of what is needed to support reliable computational load integration. As the ERO

Enterprise and industry learn more about the needs associated with computational load, criteria

(such as ride-through requirements) may need to be adjusted. Earlier in the year, the RSTC

approved a roadmap of upcoming high-priority standards development projects – with the most

urgent being the disturbance ride-through performance project mentioned above. To that end, the

ERO Enterprise requests that the Commission consider expedited evaluation of future efforts

stating that they seek to harmonize with NERC Reliability Standard requirements. NERC also

plans to request expedited Commission review of NERC’s proposed registry criteria and

                                                8
 Reliability Standards filings later this year to support clear, consistent expectations and help ensure

that foundational requirements can begin to become effective before the end of next year.

IV.    CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the reasons stated above, NERC and the Regional Entities respectfully

request that the Commission accept the comments herein.
